Definition: from a presumed compound of G1909 and G1014; a plan against someone, i.e. a plot:--laying (lying) in wait.
BiblicalUsage: Epiboule is a plot, a laying in wait — a plan made against someone in secret. The Jews lay in wait to kill Paul at Damascus, and again in Greece, and again on the road; and Paul serves the Lord with all humility of mind, and with many tears, and temptations, which befell him by the lying in wait of the Jews.
TheologicalSignificance: Every lying in wait became another road by which the gospel travelled further. I hold that the plots never once stopped the work, and Paul's tears and temptations are the proof that opposition is part of the calling, not a sign it failed.
RelatedEvents: The Plot against Paul Foiled; Paul's Farewell to the Ephesian Elders
